description: A record kept on the server and found through a random session id sent in a cookie.
A credential sent in the Authorization header that grants access to whoever presents it, so it must be protected like a password.
A short-lived token that calls the API and a longer-lived one that can only obtain new access tokens and can be revoked.
HttpOnly hides a cookie from scripts, Secure limits it to HTTPS and SameSite limits when it accompanies cross-site requests.
A Spring Security setting that never creates or uses an HTTP session, so every request must carry its own credentials.
Script-readable storage exposes tokens to XSS, while automatically attached cookies expose requests to CSRF.
A server component that holds the tokens and gives the browser only an HttpOnly session cookie.
